rules.description: Death must have occurred in England or Wales
rules.reason_if_failed: Deaths in Scotland are registered with National Records of Scotland. Deaths in Northern Ireland are registered with the General Register Office for Northern Ireland.

rules.description: Death must be registered within 5 days
rules.reason_if_failed: The death should have been registered within 5 days. Contact the register office urgently to explain the delay.

rules.description: Registrant must be a qualified informant
rules.reason_if_failed: Only certain people can register a death: a relative, someone present at the death, the occupier where the death occurred, the person arranging the funeral, or the person causing disposal of the body.

rules.description: Medical certificate of cause of death must be available
rules.reason_if_failed: You need a medical certificate of cause of death (MCCD) from a doctor before you can register the death.

edge_cases.description: Death has been referred to the coroner (sudden, unexplained, or suspicious)
edge_cases.action: Cannot register until coroner investigation is complete. The coroner will contact you when you can register. This may take weeks or months.

edge_cases.description: Baby was stillborn after 24 weeks of pregnancy
edge_cases.action: Route to stillbirth registration process. Different forms and procedures apply.
Deaths abroad must be registered according to local laws. You can also register with the UK High Commission or consulate. Use 'Register a death abroad' service.

edge_cases.description: Doctor has not issued medical certificate
edge_cases.action: Contact the doctor or hospital where the death occurred. If the death was unexpected, the coroner may need to investigate.
